groups.label: Going to work without leaving home
groups.note: Checked hardest, since a question about the start and end of the day invites talk of routine. Most of it came in answer to the day and the room (questions 2 and 3), and all six make their own way to work and back. Named from Dev's and Toby's own image of going out and coming back.
groups.description: Dev walks out of his front door 'as a man in a flat' and back in as someone at work. Toby goes out for a coffee to come back a worker, Ffion walks to the postbox in proper shoes, Ros puts on a lanyard she does not need, and Glen tells the box room 'that's you done'. None was told to do this, and most found it by trial. Where the act is skipped, work spreads: into the bed, the kitchen table, the evening email.

groups.label: Putting work out of sight
groups.description: Hiding the things of work (in a basket, a box, a drawer, behind a door or under a t-shirt) as the one end of the day that works, kept or lost by how much room a home has.

groups.label: Having to be seen to work
groups.note: Toby's account leads, so I checked it was not about youth. Glen, at sixty-three and settled, does the same with his green light at eight, and Ros with the phone in her apron.
groups.description: Out of sight of managers and colleagues, participants stand in for their own bodies at a desk: a green dot, a reply within the minute, a collared shirt. The time saved on the commute is felt as owed, a wash or a trip to the shop as being caught, and the doubt of family and neighbours ('working hard or hardly working?') confirms the need for proof. Home itself comes under the same gaze through the camera and the call.

groups.label: Lucky, so I can't complain
groups.description: Kemi has 'the thing everyone wanted', Toby was told he had won something he did not enter, Glen treats it as a favour he must prove was worth it, Ros counts her blessings beside the people at bus stops, and Dev's brother would laugh. The same debt that keeps them visible keeps them quiet.

groups.label: At home means available
groups.note: First drafted as a gendered theme. Dev's account, doing the gaps' work while his partner goes out, and Glen's, where his work takes the quiet from his wife, showed the pattern follows who is at home. Gender still shapes it (Kemi, Ros, Ffion) and the write-up should say so.
groups.description: Families, neighbours, employers and participants themselves treat 'at home' as available. Parcels, lifts, tradesmen, a sick child and an ageing parent go to the one at home, decided without discussion. The work fits into the gaps of the working day and so does not look like work, and whose job gets the room with the door settles whose job gives way.

groups.label: Missing, or glad to lose, who I was at work
groups.note: Two pulls in opposite directions, kept as one theme because what is missed and what is escaped are the same thing: the person one was at work.
groups.description: Dev misses 'Dev from testing', the ironed shirts and the people who stayed at his desk to chat, and Toby, who started in his bedroom, never got to become anyone at work. Glen, Ros and Ffion are glad to stop being that person: the banter, the drinks, being seen at a desk. Either way, who they were at work belonged to the office. The commute was part of it, time owed to nobody, which some have lost (Kemi's train) and some have found again at home (Ros's garden).

groups.label: Time that is nobody else's
groups.description: The train, the car park, the garden in the morning: ten or forty minutes in which nobody needs anything, lost with the commute or found again at home.
